title: When Bolivia's Microlender PRODEM Turned Itself Into a Bank
conflicts: Transferred book: Ohio State study (1996) says $3.96 million and about 14,300 active clients in February 1992; World Finance (BancoSol's later account) says about 17,000 clients and $4 million; story uses the study's dated figures. PRODEM founded 1986 (World Finance, MicroSave) vs began operations 1987 (Ohio State); story uses both in that sense. Founders of PRODEM described differently across sources; story names ACCION, Bolivian business leaders and the grant-makers without ranking.
notes: Built mainly on the Ohio State Rural Finance Program case study (English PDF on the Microfinance Gateway), CGAP's Focus Note, and Elisabeth Rhyne's ReVista essay. Otero's own words are available only in summary (MicroSave video page), so the story quotes Rhyne's 'radical anti-banker' instead. The divided vote is Kurt Koenigsfest's later account in World Finance, attributed. Quote stance challenges: the Dhammapada separates the road to wealth from the road to release, against BancoSol's premise that profit serves the mission; the connection leaves it unsettled.
